Definition: from G5228; insolence (as over-bearing), i.e. insult, injury:--harm, hurt, reproach.
BiblicalUsage: hýbris is the word for insolence, insult, injury. In Acts 27:10, the text says "I perceive that this voyage will be with hurt and much damage." In Acts 27:21, the text says "and to have gained this harm and loss."
TheologicalSignificance: hýbris convinces me that pride is the oldest sin, and it always ends the same way — brought low. That is why I keep this word in mind when I read those passages — it carries more than its size suggests.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
